subject: POC kickoff: prompt review, routing & load-test windows
messages:
From: Alex Weaver <alex@quantum-retail.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@quantum-retail.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC: Hands-on prompt workshop — scheduling + guardrails

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at Quantum Retail would like to move forward with a short POC and a hands-on prompt review workshop. High level asks from our side: a 3-hour working session for prompt inventory + structured-output requirements, a separate 1-hour session to validate routing and hit fallbacks, and a short load-test window (30 minutes) to verify throughput for our peak storefront queries.

Can you share availability the week of Apr 19 and the week of Apr 26? Prefer mornings Pacific (we're based in SF). Also attaching a quick prompt inventory template so our ML engineer can start populating.

Attachments: prompt-inventory-template.csv (stub)

Thanks,
Alex Weaver
Head of AI 
Quantum Retail
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Weaver <alex@quantum-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC: Hands-on prompt workshop — scheduling + guardrails

Hi Alex — great to hear, super excited to run this with your team. Proposed plan below and a couple of asks so we can come prepared: 

Proposed kickoff + hands-on schedule (3 total sessions):
- Day 1 (3h): Prompt inventory walkthrough + structured-output requirements (guardrails, success metrics)
- Day 2 (1h): Routing & fallbacks (model variants, latency SLOs)
- Day 3 (30m): Load-test window (simulated peak traffic)

Preferred slots (all PT):
- Week of Apr 19: Tue 4/20 09:00–12:00 or Thu 4/22 09:00–12:00
- Week of Apr 26: Tue 4/27 09:00–12:00 or Wed 4/28 09:00–12:00

Please confirm a preferred slot and our team will lock calendar invites. A few asks so the session is high signal:
- Please upload a completed prompt-inventory-template.csv to the shared Drive (link below) at least 48 hours before the hands-on session.
- Identify 3 representative prompts for the load test (we'll need expected token lengths and sample payloads).
- Call out any regulatory/PII guardrails we should enforce during testing (redaction rules, retention limits).

Attaching a rough agenda (poc-agenda-v1.pdf) — we'll iterate once you pick a date.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/example-prompt-inventory

Attachments: poc-agenda-v1.pdf (stub)

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Cc: Alex Weaver <alex@quantum-retail.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC: Hands-on prompt workshop — scheduling + guardrails

Looping in a couple of quick notes from infra/ops perspective: 

- For the load test please confirm desired QPS and concurrency targets. We typically recommend a stepped run (10min ramp, 10min steady, 10min ramp-down) to capture cache warming behavior.
- We'll prepare a routing matrix example that shows cost vs latency trade-offs for the variants we'll propose.
- Suggest we include a short section on structured-output validation (schemas + automated checks) — saves time during the workshop.

If Alex confirms a date we can provision a dedicated load-test pool and share credentials for the simulated traffic generator.

Ben
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
